races.name: Betway Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Rogue Millions
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 266-day break but has winning C&D form and benefits from gelding operation
runners_data.spotlight: Highly impressive C&D winner (soft ground; handles good) on handicap debut last June; didn't build on that in two subsequent runs but has been gelded and switched stables; still low-mileage and his new yard has been among the winners; fascinating contender.

runners_data.name: Dancing In Paris
runners_data.note: Closer with solid staying form but major concern over 266-day absence for Ian Williams
runners_data.spotlight: A third runner for Ian Williams; ran some fine races in defeat last season, including at Glorious Goodwood (1m6f, good to soft); returns after nine months off over a trip probably short of his optimum.

runners_data.name: Castle Stuart
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who shaped like he wanted further at York, gets ideal trip here with recent runs under belt
runners_data.spotlight: Respectable sixth over 1m2f both starts this year, the latter in a warm race at York when shaping as if worth another try over 1m3f+; gets that here and has each-way hopes.

runners_data.name: Claymore
runners_data.note: Natural leader but 4lb higher than last win and returning from poor Dubai form, questions over current ability
runners_data.spotlight: Campaigned in the UAE this winter, last seen finishing tailed off at Meydan; still 4lb higher than for his last win in Britain and probably best watched after three months off.

runners_data.name: Humble Spark
runners_data.note: Tough hold-up horse with good recent form, Lauren Young's 5lb claim valuable at the weights
runners_data.spotlight: Tough 6yo with seven wins to his name; beaten favourite at Hamilton (1m3f, good) last time but shaped quite nicely, keeping on into second place after a slow start and meeting trouble; place possibilities again at the very least.

runners_data.name: Per Contra
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with habit of slow starts, needs to overcome tardy beginning to be competitive
runners_data.comment: Won at Newcastle last autumn but hasn't repeated the form; slow starts becoming a habit
runners_data.spotlight: Won off 2lb lower at Newcastle last autumn but hasn't repeated the form and slow starts are becoming a habit; needs to get back on track.

runners_data.name: Topteam
runners_data.note: Front-runner with William Buick up, good recent form including C&D second suggests ready for another bold show
runners_data.comment: Four wins from 11 starts; good second at Newmarket last time; in the mix once more
runners_data.spotlight: Four wins from 11 starts; successful on comeback at Kempton (1m4f, AW; made all) in April and again ran well when second at Newmarket (1m4f, good) two weeks ago; should be in the thick of things once more.

runners_data.name: Ghaiyya
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has won twice this season, consistent front-running style suits track configuration
runners_data.spotlight: Likeable front-running filly; made a winning return at Doncaster (1m4f, good to firm) and typically gave her all when second at Hamilton (1m5f, good) three weeks later; edging up the weights but set for another bold show.

runners_data.name: Star Harbour
runners_data.note: Irish-trained hold-up horse on long losing run, hard to recommend despite Adrian McGuinness handling
runners_data.spotlight: Irish-trained 8yo, on a long losing sequence; not entirely disgraced when fourth of ten at Leopardstown (1m4f, good) two weeks ago; others have more potential but he's certainly well treated on his best form.

runners_data.name: Real Dream
runners_data.note: Prominent type carrying top weight of 138lbs, hasn't beaten a rival in two British runs this year
runners_data.spotlight: Fourth in handicap in Saudi Arabia on second start this year but has not beaten a rival in two runs back in Britain; difficult to recommend.

runners_data.name: Enemy
runners_data.note: Hold-up veteran returning to turf after AW wins, beaten soundly last time and faces stronger opposition
runners_data.spotlight: Durable veteran who won twice on the AW early this year; however, he was soundly beaten at Newcastle on Good Friday and faces some unexposed rivals on his return to turf.

runners_data.name: Tiernan
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose Listed third at Hamilton looks anomalous form, hard to trust at current level
runners_data.spotlight: Close third of seven in Listed event at Hamilton (1m3f, good; 150-1) last summer, but that run stands out like a sore thumb from the rest of his form and he was well beaten (after wind surgery) over the same C&D on reappearance; too much to prove for comfort.

runners_data.name: Opportunity
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced closer returning from 11-month break, showed promise at Ascot but needs to build on comeback
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly raced 4yo; good fourth in Listed race at Goodwood last spring; gelded and off 11 months, shaped promisingly when third of 14 on handicap debut at Ascot (1m4f, good to firm) three weeks ago, doing his best work late on; nudged up 1lb but still looks seriously unexposed; strong claims.

races.paceDynamic: Claymore and Topteam will ensure a genuine pace from the front, with Ghaiyya likely to press them from a prominent position early. The confirmed pace angle from two natural leaders should create an honest gallop over this stamina-testing 1m3f trip, with the tempo likely sustained rather than stop-start given both front-runners' styles. With multiple hold-up horses including Rogue Millions, Dancing In Paris, and Opportunity looking to finish strongly, the combination of genuine pace and the testing distance strongly favours closers who can deliver their challenge late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Claymore and Topteam go too hard early and Ghaiyya presses them
scenarios.body: The genuine pace will stretch the field and create the perfect setup for hold-up horses to deliver telling late runs. Patient tactics will be rewarded as the pace-setters weaken in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tactical Battle Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If one of the pace-setters drops out early leaving moderate tempo
scenarios.body: Without sustained pressure, the race becomes more tactical and suits horses that can position closer to the pace. Prominent racers and those with tactical speed gain the advantage.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Topteam or Claymore gets an easy lead with controlled fractions
scenarios.body: The leader can dictate terms and kick clear when the pace lifts, making it difficult for closers to reel them in. Class and stamina reserves prove decisive from the front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Stamina Slog Develops
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is moderate but the tempo gradually builds
scenarios.body: The race becomes a true staying test where stamina and recent fitness matter most. Horses with proven form at the trip and regular racing gain the edge.

watchPoints.text: Claymore and Topteam could go too fast early if both commit to leading, burning each other out
Multiple Ian Williams runners in Real Dream, Dancing In Paris and Enemy may struggle with trainer's current form
Rogue Millions and Dancing In Paris both return from 266-day breaks, fitness could be major factor
Per Contra's habit of slow starts could prove costly in a race likely to be run at genuine pace
Opportunity's fitness after 11-month break and gelding operation, debut for Haggas worth noting

races.name: Betway Reverence Handicap

runners_data.name: Jordan Electrics
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who fades late but drops 7lbs from his Victoria Cup effort and has Tom Marquand's booking
runners_data.spotlight: Spent last year in the grip of the handicapper after seven wins in 2024; more leniently treated now and ran respectably when sixth of 28 in the 7f Victoria Cup at Ascot; seemed unsuited by drop back to 5f next time; this intermediate trip is probably ideal these days and he commands respect.

runners_data.name: Dark Cloud Rising
runners_data.note: Natural pace-setter who can press Station X early but hasn't fired this season and needs to rediscover 2025 form
runners_data.spotlight: Had a solid 2025, winning three times (5f/6f), but hasn't finished in the first eight this year; dropping in the weights but needs to turn a corner; perhaps a change of headgear will help.

runners_data.name: Brosay
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with back-to-back wins last year but will need significant luck from his deep position in this big field
runners_data.spotlight: Back-to-back 6f wins at Windsor (good to firm) and Ascot (good to soft) in 2025; has taken a while to get going this season but he shaped as if coming to the boil when sixth of 14 at Newbury (led briefly over 1f out) two weeks ago; back to his last winning mark and should be at concert pitch now.

runners_data.name: Mister Sox
runners_data.note: Proven at this level but 8th at York last week suggests he's still above his optimum handicap mark
runners_data.spotlight: His six successes include four last season; retains all his ability but he's still above his last winning mark and he was only eighth at York last Saturday.

runners_data.name: Station X
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner who gets perfect setup as sole pace-setter and showed career-best form at Southwell in April
runners_data.comment: Front-runner; followed Southwell win with close sixth at Hamilton; in the mix again
runners_data.spotlight: Front-runner who posted a career best when seeing off five rivals at Southwell (6f) in April; beaten only narrowly when sixth in blanket finish at Hamilton (5f, good) last time; reliable, and should be in the mix again.

runners_data.name: Fivethousandtoone
runners_data.note: Struggles on turf with 1-27 record and 35 days off suggests he needs this run back on grass
runners_data.spotlight: Four-time AW winner, only 1-27 on grass; never the slightest threat on return to turf at Leicester; others have more convincing profiles.

runners_data.name: Recency Bias
runners_data.note: Progressive 4yo who travels strongly but stepping back to 6f from 7f wins may not suit his style
runners_data.spotlight: Unexposed 4yo with a progressive profile; beaten neck when odds-on at Newcastle (7f) last month; usually travels strongly and should be at least as effective back at 6f; still on a workable mark and high on the list.

runners_data.name: Marty Hopkirk
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who shaped better behind Redorange at Windsor and can track the early pace
runners_data.spotlight: Unplaced in last four handicaps but there was more encouragement in his fourth to Redorange (runs in the Listed race at 2.33) at Windsor 12 days ago; has raced mainly at 5f but should stay further; not without hope.

runners_data.name: Realign
runners_data.note: All-or-nothing performer who bolted up at Haydock but 45 days off and needs everything to fall right
runners_data.comment: Bolted up at Haydock last autumn; might have needed reappearance; strongly considered
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly raced 4yo with something of an all-or-nothing profile; put everything together when bolting up at Haydock (6f, good to soft) last autumn; might have needed the run when only ninth of 13 at Newmarket on reappearance; leading claims if building on that and cheekpieces may give him a lift.

runners_data.name: Grant Wood
runners_data.note: Consistent performer at 7yo who went close at Ripon but faces stronger opposition here
runners_data.spotlight: Almost as good as ever at the age of seven and went down narrowly at Ripon (6f, good) earlier this month; hard to knock but this is a warm race and he faces some unexposed rivals.

runners_data.name: Wild Clary
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with class but found only Realign too strong last time and needs clear run
runners_data.spotlight: Found only Realign too strong at Haydock (6f, good to soft) last autumn despite meeting trouble at a crucial stage, and he was back on the up when a neck second of 16 at Ripon (6f, good to soft) six weeks ago; reliable and has notably solid credentials.

runners_data.name: Rousing Encore
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who met trouble at York and needs cleaner passage to show true form
runners_data.spotlight: Promising second on reappearance at Newcastle and better than the bare results suggest since, meeting significant trouble in running in a big field at York last time; could play a major role if getting the breaks.

runners_data.name: Gressington
runners_data.note: Out of sorts since December and 40-1 at York suggests confidence is low despite weight drop
runners_data.comment: Out of sorts since December win; beginning to look well handicapped but needs a revival
runners_data.spotlight: Out of sorts since December AW success, finishing in midfield at York (40-1) on return to turf last time; beginning to look well handicapped but needs a revival.

runners_data.name: Havana Rum
runners_data.note: 6lb above last winning mark and disappointing at Doncaster after promising Pontefract return
runners_data.spotlight: Went close at Pontefract (5f, good to soft) on reappearance but had no obvious excuses at Doncaster next time; more exposed than some of these and 6lb above his highest winning mark.

runners_data.name: Native Honey
runners_data.note: Surged back to form with 7f Ayr win 10 days ago and low weight gives competitive chance
runners_data.spotlight: Both wins have come over 7f at Ayr, and he surged back to form when scoring there ten days ago; still lightly raced, in excellent hands, and should be at least as effective over this trip on a stiff track; a danger to all at the foot of the weights.

races.paceDynamic: Station X is the sole confirmed front-runner and should get an easy lead with no pressure from the 15-runner field. Jordan Electrics, Dark Cloud Rising, and Marty Hopkirk will settle prominently behind him, but none are natural pace-pressers over 6f. The large field means the hold-up horses like Brosay, Mister Sox, Realign, and Wild Clary will be buried deep and need significant luck in running. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and the lone leader Station X, as the sustainable pace and congested finish will make it difficult for horses coming from the back to make up ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Station X Controls All
scenarios.trigger: If Station X gets an uncontested lead and kicks clear in the final furlong
scenarios.body: The front-runner's sustainable gallop leaves him with enough in reserve to hold off late challengers, while the packed field behind struggles for racing room. His career-best Southwell win shows he can dominate when allowed to dictate.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Jordan Electrics or Dark Cloud Rising track Station X closely and pounce late
scenarios.body: The experienced Jordan Electrics uses his class to time his challenge perfectly, or Dark Cloud Rising's early pace helps him strike from a handy position. Both avoid the traffic problems that will plague the hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Hero Gets Luck
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses and gaps appear for the closers in the final 2f
scenarios.body: Brosay or Wild Clary benefit from their class and get the clear run they need to unleash their finishing kicks. The moderate early pace allows them to close the gap despite their deep positions.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Finish Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses get severely hampered and an outsider finds daylight
scenarios.body: The 15-runner field creates a cavalry charge finish where positioning trumps ability. Native Honey or Grant Wood benefit from being in the right place when others are blocked.

watchPoints.text: Station X could steal this if he gets the expected uncontested lead and sustainable fractions that leave him with energy to kick clear
Jordan Electrics drops 7lbs from his Victoria Cup run and his prominent style could be perfectly placed to strike behind the leader
The 15-runner field will create significant traffic problems for hold-up horses like Brosay and Wild Clary who need clear runs
Native Honey's recent 7f Ayr win suggests he's back in form and his 9lb weight advantage could be crucial in a tight finish
Dark Cloud Rising showed early pace in his wins last season but needs to bounce back from a disappointing 2024 campaign

races.name: Betway Achilles Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Rogue Lightning
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse faces traffic concerns over 5f trip, but globetrotting form including Qatar win shows he handles good ground well
runners_data.spotlight: Globetrotting gelding whose last win came in Qatar (6f, good) in February 2025 when Washington Heights was second; has run respectably on his two outings this season, fourth in French Group 3 (5f, soft) on latest; should be thereabouts under optimum conditions.

runners_data.name: Washington Heights
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose Listed-winning form at York gives him course/distance edge, though four poor runs this season are concerning
runners_data.spotlight: Close third in Group 2 Temple Stakes at Haydock 12 months ago and made most to win Listed race at York (5f, good to firm) last summer; well below par all four starts since (short of room in Newmarket Group 3 on latest) but down in grade here and may well bounce back.

runners_data.name: Starlust
runners_data.note: Class act returning from 347-day break with Grade 1 Breeders' Cup form, but hold-up style problematic over minimum trip
runners_data.spotlight: Top-class form when third in Group 1 Nunthorpe at York and when winning Grade 1 Breeders' Cup Turf Sprint at Del Mar, both in 2024; rusty on last year's reappearance but showed he retains plenty of ability when fourth of 20 in Group 1 King Charles III at Royal Ascot on only subsequent outing; leading claims if showing his best after layoff, although that's not guaranteed.

runners_data.name: Celandine
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner gets tactical advantage as sole leader, though 0-6 record since 2yo Group 2 win raises reliability questions
runners_data.spotlight: 0-6 since winning the Group 2 Lowther (6f, good to firm) as a 2yo, although she had an excuse (awkward leaving stalls, never a threat) in 6f Listed event at Newmarket (13-2) on reappearance; below par on two previous attempts at 5f, but not ruled out if on a going day for in-form yard.

runners_data.name: Redorange
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in sharp form after Windsor success 12 days ago, wears tongue-tie and has strong record on good ground
runners_data.spotlight: Classy sprinter who built on an eye-catching reappearance when justifying strong support in handicap at Windsor (5f, good) 12 days ago; found only one too good in French Listed event last summer and looks a strong contender back in this grade.

runners_data.name: Azure Angel
runners_data.note: Late-running mare whose 22-1 Bath Listed success proves she can strike at this level, but needs luck in running over 5f
runners_data.spotlight: 6yo mare who sprang a 22-1 surprise in Listed race at Bath (5f, good) in April, swooping fast and late; likeable type with an impressive strike-rate but she'll need another personal best under a penalty.

runners_data.name: Ten Pounds
runners_data.note: Prominent runner struggling since stable switch, with headgear changes suggesting connections searching for improvement
runners_data.comment: Unplaced all four outings since joining current stable and is unproven at 5f
runners_data.spotlight: 5-10 at 6f/7f for Harry Charlton; unplaced all four outings since joining current stable, finishing in midfield in Victoria Cup at Ascot most recently; unproven at 5f; wears headgear for the first time; others appeal more.

runners_data.name: Luna A Inbhir Nis
runners_data.note: Front-running type from 0-from-10 trainer, but progressive 2024 campaign including York handicap win shows ability
runners_data.spotlight: Front-runner; most progressive last season, making it six wins for the campaign in handicap at York (5.4f, good) in July;  probably needed the run when down the field there on reappearance; stiffer task up in grade.

races.paceDynamic: Celandine will take the field along as the sole confirmed front-runner, with Washington Heights and Ten Pounds likely settling prominently behind her. The presence of just one natural leader means Celandine can dictate terms without pressure, creating a moderate tempo that builds gradually. With multiple hold-up horses including Rogue Lightning, Starlust, Redorange and Azure Angel needing room to maneuver in the short 5f trip, traffic problems are inevitable. This race shape strongly favors front-running and prominent racers who can avoid the scramble and capitalize on a controlled pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Front Runner
scenarios.trigger: If Celandine gets an easy lead with minimal early pressure
scenarios.body: She can control fractions perfectly and kick clear when ready, while the hold-up brigade gets caught in traffic behind a strung-out field. The 4yo filly's class edge from her Group 2 Lowther win becomes decisive when she doesn't have to work hard early.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Hero Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes genuinely strong or Celandine stops quickly
scenarios.body: The closers get the perfect setup to unleash their finishing kicks, with Redorange's recent Windsor win showing his current sharpness. Either Starlust's class or Redorange's form momentum proves decisive in a cavalry charge finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Washington Heights or Ten Pounds track the leader perfectly and pounce
scenarios.body: They get first run on the leaders while avoiding the traffic that snares the hold-up horses behind. Washington Heights' Listed-winning form at this trip gives him the edge if he can find his old spark.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If severe interference occurs in the final furlong creating gaps
scenarios.body: Azure Angel or another hold-up horse finds a dream passage through the carnage while others are stopped in their tracks. The 22-1 Bath Listed winner's late kick becomes unstoppable with clear room.

watchPoints.text: Celandine must break cleanly given her front-running style and awkward start excuse at Newmarket last time
Traffic problems developing in final furlong where multiple hold-up horses including Starlust and Redorange need room simultaneously
Washington Heights's early position crucial as prominent runner needs to avoid getting squeezed between leader and hold-up horses
Redorange and Azure Angel both need significant pace on to be effective, but genuine speed may not materialize
Luna A Inbhir Nis showing any early speed could disrupt Celandine's uncontested lead scenario

races.name: Betway Lester Piggott Fillies' Stakes (Group 3) (Formerly Known As The Pinnacle Stakes)

runners_data.name: Estrange
runners_data.note: Defending champion returning after 224 days but holds clear class edge with Group 1 form, hold-up style suits expected pace scenario
runners_data.spotlight: Very talented 5yo whose two wins last year included this race (1m4f, good; at Haydock) on reappearance; ran a cracker when second in Group 1 at Ascot (1m4f, good) on final start; that makes her the clear form pick back in this grade and she's the one to beat if ready to roll after 224 days off.

runners_data.name: Waardah
runners_data.note: Stablemate of leader but brings superior staying credentials from Goodwood Group 2 win, dangerous closer if ready after long break
runners_data.spotlight: Stablemate of Azaniya; seemed to relish the step up to 1m6f when winning the Group 2 Lillie Langtry at Goodwood (good to soft) last summer; didn't give her running in Group 1 at Ascot on final 3yo start, finishing well behind Estrange; may still have untapped potential but this trip looks a bare minimum.

runners_data.name: Azaniya
runners_data.note: Only front-runner faces tactical pressure making all the running over this trip despite recent Saint-Cloud success showing ability
runners_data.spotlight: Progressed well last season, her four wins from just five outings culminating in a clearcut Listed success at Saint-Cloud (1m2f, heavy; also handles good to firm); shaped as if needing the run when fifth in Group 3 there on reappearance; gives the impression she'll relish this extra yardage, and with further improvement on the cards she's high on the list.

runners_data.name: Crepe Suzette
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with Doncaster Group 2 form but disappointing last time, needs career-best to win this
runners_data.spotlight: Ended her 3yo campaign with an excellent third in Doncaster's Group 2 Park Hill Stakes (14.5f, good to soft); bit disappointing when only fifth in Listed race at Goodwood (11-8 favourite; beaten over 7l by Coedana) on return; now on a retrieval mission in first-time headgear.

runners_data.name: Coedana
runners_data.note: Progressive closer who ran career-best second at Goodwood last time, form trending sharply upward for in-form Edward Bethell yard
runners_data.spotlight: Improving with virtually every run, and was even better than the bare result when second in Listed race at Goodwood (1m4f, good; came from a long way back) four weeks ago; up in grade again but still has more in the tank and not to be underestimated.

runners_data.name: Sharpen
runners_data.note: Sole prominent runner after 242-day break, new stable acquisition for George Boughey who excels with horses returning from layoffs
runners_data.spotlight: Sole win in Ireland came in 1m2f maiden but she was also a good second in a 1m4f Listed event; changed hands for 360,000gns in December; plenty of improvement required on British debut but she has switched to a flourishing stable and is not without hope.

runners_data.name: Patagonia Girl
runners_data.note: Recent Chester handicap winner stepping into Group company for first time, likely outclassed despite progressive profile
runners_data.spotlight: Has made incremental progress over 11 starts, overcoming a wide draw when beating 14 rivals in handicap at Chester (1m4f, good) three weeks ago; may be open to further improvement but that win came off a mark of just 80 and this is a significantly stiffer assignment.

runners_data.name: Naga
runners_data.note: Hat-trick winner earlier this season but held-up style requires perfect setup, Gosden stable in excellent form currently
runners_data.spotlight: Completed a hat-trick of handicap wins at Doncaster (1m2f, good to firm) in April and did well in the circumstances when a never-nearer third at Ascot last month; rises steeply in grade here but still has untapped potential.

races.paceDynamic: Azaniya is the sole confirmed front-runner and will dictate terms from flag to finish without pressure, creating a steady, sustainable gallop over this stamina-testing 1m3f trip. With six hold-up horses (Estrange, Waardah, Crepe Suzette, Coedana, Patagonia Girl, Naga) and only Sharpen likely to sit handy, the pace will be moderate early before quickening from the 3f pole. This controlled tempo strongly favours the closers who can unleash late kicks, while the uncontested leader Azaniya faces the tactical disadvantage of making all the running over this demanding distance.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Closers Dominate Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays moderate as expected with Azaniya controlling the tempo
scenarios.body: The strong group of hold-up horses get the perfect setup to unleash devastating late runs in the final 2f. Estrange and Waardah have the class and finishing kicks to exploit this scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Stays Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Azaniya sets fractions fast enough to discourage closers or they get locked in traffic
scenarios.body: The uncontested leader builds a decisive advantage turning for home and holds off the late challengers. Azaniya's recent Saint-Cloud win shows she can make all effectively when allowed to dictate.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mid-Division Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and Sharpen can position perfectly in behind Azaniya
scenarios.body: The prominent runner gets first run on the field from an ideal tracking position while the hold-up horses are caught flat-footed. Sharpen's trainer George Boughey excels with horses returning from breaks.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Fractures Field
scenarios.trigger: If Azaniya goes too fast early or the hold-up horses spread wide turning for home
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish between whatever horses have conserved energy best regardless of running style. Form horses with tactical speed like Naga and Patagonia Girl can capitalise on the chaos.

watchPoints.text: Azaniya sets unsustainable fractions early as the lone leader, compromising her stamina reserves for the finish
Estrange shows any signs of rustiness after 224-day absence despite being defending champion with superior class
Sharpen gets prominent position behind Azaniya as the only horse likely to track the leader closely
Traffic problems develop in the straight with six hold-up horses all needing room simultaneously
Waardah and Azaniya as stablemates create tactical complications for Owen Burrows with conflicting running styles

races.name: Betway Silver Bowl Handicap (Heritage Handicap)

runners_data.name: Laureate Crown
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with strong recent form, 36 days since last run could be ideal for peak fitness
runners_data.comment: Launched late bids from the back for two 1m wins this term; travelled well last time
runners_data.spotlight: Won on good to firm on debut; gelded before taking a small-field handicap at Wolverhampton (8.6f, AW) in March and he improved again to follow up at Sandown (1m, good) five weeks ago; launched late bids from the back for those 2026 wins, travelled well last time and could have more left in the tank.

runners_data.name: Princling
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with Tom Marquand aboard, excellent recent reappearance suggests ready to strike
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up last October on both 2yo starts (7f, AW/good), on the second occasion in a novice at Newmarket that has worked out very well; reappeared with a ready win at 1-4 in Wetherby novice (1m, good to firm) and there's every chance that this unexposed colt will be better than today's opening mark.

runners_data.name: Archer Royal
runners_data.note: Hold-up style but 63-day break is concerning for immediate fitness needs
runners_data.comment: Well held last two starts; first headgear for handicap debut needs to prompt vastly better
runners_data.spotlight: Won debut (7f, AW) and came third in Group 3 at Newmarket (7f, good) last September; however, he was last of seven in another Group 3 there (1m, good to firm) on final 2yo outing and beaten 10l in a conditions stakes at Kempton (1m, AW) on March reappearance; the latter was a hot race but today's first-time headgear for handicap debut needs to prompt a vastly better show.

runners_data.name: Langstone
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in excellent form with two recent wins, gelding operation has transformed him
runners_data.comment: 2-2 this term in novice events; promising and probably has an advantageous opening mark
runners_data.spotlight: Gelded after debut and has left sole that 2yo run (6f, soft) well behind him by winning novice events at Doncaster (7f, good to soft) and Kempton (7f, AW) this spring; did well to score with strong finish last time, having been carried left; promising and probably has an advantageous mark for this handicap debut, especially now upped in trip.

runners_data.name: Blue Courvoisier
runners_data.note: Forward-going type who has found his feet in handicaps, good record on this going
runners_data.spotlight: Reappeared with close second on handicap debut at Newmarket (1m, good) last month, followed by a respectable fourth of 11 at Ascot (1m, good; favourite); has had only four races but probably needs to resume improvement.

runners_data.name: Daydreama
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who needs strong pace, best efforts have come from off the speed at York
runners_data.comment: Second of 14 from well off pace at York (7f) 17 days ago; has to be worth a go beyond 7f
runners_data.spotlight: Won two novice events last summer; easily best of his six efforts since have both been from well off the pace over 7f on good ground at York, including his second in 14-runner race 17 days ago; back up 2lb but has to be worth a go beyond 7f (dam 2m winner) and needs a second look.

runners_data.name: Sponsor
runners_data.note: Front-runner wearing tongue-tie, will ensure honest gallop but may pay for early exertions
runners_data.spotlight: Tongue tied when showing significant ability on all three starts, on last two occasions taking minor honours in novice events at Windsor (1m, good to firm) and Newbury (7f, good); needs better on this handicap debut but these are early days and his stable has had recent 3yo winners.

runners_data.name: Sir Albert
runners_data.note: Prominent racer carrying top weight but 7lb claimer Alfie Redman provides valuable assistance
runners_data.comment: Close Listed 5th at Lingfield (7f, AW) in February; 7lb claimer is recruited; 1m may help
runners_data.spotlight: 2-2 in nurseries last July (7f, good/heavy) and close Listed fifth at Lingfield (7f, AW) this February; has top weight in this hot handicap but 7lb claimer is recruited and the step up to nearly 1m may help.

runners_data.name: Suspended Sentence
runners_data.note: Forward-going horse who may have needed his comeback run last time out
runners_data.comment: May have needed last month's comeback behind Laureate Crown but not obviously well treated
runners_data.spotlight: Progressive once upped to 1m as 2yo, winning twice (good to firm/soft) before his Listed fourth in France (soft); may have needed last month's comeback run in the race won by Laureate Crown at Sandown (1m, good to firm; 14-1 from 20-1) but he's not obviously well treated.

runners_data.name: Inishbeg
runners_data.note: Prominent type with 5lb claimer aboard, disappointed on handicap debut but better expected
runners_data.comment: Made most when below form on handicap debut at York (7f, good) but was drawn widest
runners_data.spotlight: Fourth attempt when winning a Thirsk maiden (7f, good) in April; made most when below form on handicap debut at York (7f, good) 17 days ago, which can probably be forgiven from widest draw and he was second favourite that day; 5lb claimer is recruited for this hot race on first crack at about 1m.

runners_data.name: Crest Of Fire
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from 65-day break, trainer Jack Channon has poor recent record
runners_data.comment: Beaten a neck on nursery debut and runaway AW maiden winner on return; looks well treated
runners_data.spotlight: Made the running when beaten a neck on nursery debut at Doncaster (1m, good to soft) last September, which was the second leg of a four-timer for the winner; reappeared with an easy 10l win at 2-5 in a maiden at Southwell (1m, AW; made all) in March and looks well treated today, given that his mark is unaltered since that win.

runners_data.name: Lake Como
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who hasn't transferred AW form to turf handicaps convincingly
runners_data.comment: Peak AW form was not transferred to 1m turf handicaps last two starts; this track may help
runners_data.spotlight: Found serious improvement over 7f/1m on AW but, although running respectably, he's not transferred the best of that form to 1m turf handicaps on last two outings (good to firm/good); this stiffer track may suit.

runners_data.name: Special Dividend
runners_data.note: Front-runner making seasonal debut after 247-day absence, fitness must be questioned
runners_data.spotlight: Won last summer on first two starts (6f, AW) then kept on for third of 18 in nursery at York (7f, good to firm) that worked out nicely; well beaten in Newmarket Group 3 (7f, good) on final 2yo start, which was followed by wind and gelding operations this March; also now has a first-time tongue-tie; needs to resume improvement in a major way.

runners_data.name: Astrazar
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who found improvement when stepped up in trip, suited by strong pace
runners_data.spotlight: Won Ffos Las maiden (7.3f, heavy) last September on seventh start, when going beyond 6f for first time, and he followed up in last-gasp fashion in valuable EBF Final at York (7f, good); denied a clear run when mid-division in handicap at Newbury (7f, good; 12-1) on reappearance and the step up to nearly 1m looks a very good move; one to note.

runners_data.name: Delinquent
runners_data.note: Prominent racer in excellent form with recent wins, progressive type moving through the ranks
runners_data.spotlight: Won 1m handicaps at Southwell (AW) in April and Hamilton (good; 6lb higher today) 15 days ago; that's two wins from eight starts and he should be a lot more exposed than most of today's rivals, but he was firmly in charge in first-time cheekpieces on that latest outing.

runners_data.name: Synners Kid
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse wearing tongue-tie, mixed recent form but has shown ability in the past
runners_data.comment: Dual Irish 1m winner as 2yo; needs to better recent British debut but tongue-tie returns
runners_data.spotlight: Won nursery debut for Joseph O'Brien at Naas (1m, yielding to soft) last September and easily followed up at Bellewstown (1m, soft), both in a tongue-tie; having shot up the weights he reappeared with sixth of ten when 66-1 for stable debut at Ascot (7f, good) three weeks ago, which is his highest rating; could build on that (as he needs to) with tongue-tie reapplied this time.

races.paceDynamic: Special Dividend and Sponsor will contest the early lead in this 16-runner handicap, with both confirmed front-runners likely to ensure a genuine gallop from the start. The large field means prominent racers like Princling, Blue Courvoisier, and Suspended Sentence will also be positioned handy to the pace, creating a competitive early tempo. This honest pace will set up perfectly for the hold-up horses to deliver their challenge, as the early leaders will have done plenty of work in the opening exchanges. The race shape strongly favours horses with hold-up styles who can finish from off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Early Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Special Dividend and Sponsor go hard from the flag and maintain a strong gallop
scenarios.body: The early leaders will weaken in the final furlong, allowing closers to sweep past with superior finishing kicks. Hold-up horses like Laureate Crown and Daydreama benefit from the strong pace collapse.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tactical Battle
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes more measured with neither leader wanting to make the running
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish with prominent racers and those with tactical speed holding sway. Horses like Princling and Blue Courvoisier can dictate from their forward positions.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Breakaway Success
scenarios.trigger: If one of the front-runners gets an easy lead and controls the fractions
scenarios.body: The leader maintains enough energy to hold off late challengers in a front-running success. Special Dividend or Sponsor could exploit their pace advantage if allowed soft fractions early.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Wide Open Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is chaotic with multiple horses vying for position throughout
scenarios.body: The race becomes a scramble where any horse can win regardless of running style. Form horses with recent fitness and good jockeys become crucial factors.

watchPoints.text: Special Dividend's fitness after 247 days off the track could see him fade quickly if setting strong pace
Archer Royal and Crest Of Fire both return from lengthy breaks and may need the run for future targets
Watch the early pace battle between Special Dividend and Sponsor as it will determine the race shape
Blue Courvoisier's market position will indicate connections' confidence after recent Ascot disappointment
Sir Albert carries top weight and needs Alfie Redman's 7lb claim to prove decisive in this competitive heat

races.name: Betway Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Albaydaa
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with classy connections who should relish any pace scenario given her finishing kick
runners_data.spotlight: Classy pedigree; ready winner when upped to 7f (AW) on final 2yo start; pleasing comeback at Newmarket (6f) in April, when a keeping-on third of 13, just ahead of a subsequent Listed winner; unfortunate to run up against a big improver at Ascot (7f, good) since but aims lower here; solid.

runners_data.name: Distant Shore
runners_data.note: Hold-up type wearing headgear for the second time with solid Varian stable backing over this ideal trip
runners_data.spotlight: Hooded both starts; never raced smoothly from the word go on Salisbury debut (6f) so did well to force a dead-heat on the line; looked more professional when third under a penalty at Thirsk (7f; also good to firm) four weeks ago and this stiffer test at the trip can suit; should improve.

runners_data.name: Jannas Journey
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner having first course experience but returning to last year's winning distance after mixed 2026 form
runners_data.spotlight: Had a wonderful 2025, winning seven times at 6f-1m on a range of surfaces; not much to celebrate this year, and this is her first course run, but back on her last winning mark and a revival should come at some stage.

runners_data.name: Fouette
runners_data.note: Strong hold-up horse stepping back down in grade after being highly tried in Listed company recently
runners_data.spotlight: Back from absence with two 7f AW wins last autumn, then set fire to her mark by running well in Listed events; highly tried on first two starts in 2026 before running quite promisingly at Goodwood (7f, good; first turf handicap) last week, considering she never had a clear run; can fare better.

runners_data.name: Orchid
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer wearing tongue-tie who may struggle for stamina over this 7f trip based on recent form
runners_data.spotlight: Both wins at 6f on the AW, either side of a winter break as a 2yo and 3yo; seemingly had stamina limitations back over 7f in the autumn and, while she should come on for her recent reappearance at Newmarket, this is a stiff track on which to prove her staying power.

runners_data.name: Lady Kodiac
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who has been respectable rather than dynamic in 3yo handicaps this season
runners_data.spotlight: Made most for two 6f novice wins on Chelmsford AW as 2yo; respectable rather than dynamic efforts as 3yo, including in a 6f Newmarket handicap last time behind a wide-margin winner who had no pretensions to being way ahead of her mark; needs improvement for step up to 7f.

runners_data.name: Applesandpears
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who raced clear in AW wins but struggled when stepped up to 1m last time
runners_data.comment: Won final two juvenile starts on AW; well held in turf handicap on return; can do better
runners_data.spotlight: Raced clear in 7f and 6f events on the AW last autumn but she was slightly hampered and done with from a fair way out on her handicap debut at Haydock (1m, good); should come on for the run, though, and no surprise if she shows to better advantage in a less competitive race.

runners_data.name: Just A Girl
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who has been consistent without winning since handicapping began this year
runners_data.spotlight: Wide-margin winner of a Lingfield novice (about 7f, good) last August but she's been on much the same mark, with little reward, since handicapping and a recent second at Newmarket was a remote one; needs weight off back.

runners_data.name: Ziggy's Queen
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer wearing headgear who showed winter AW form but struggled on turf return
runners_data.spotlight: Two narrow AW wins at 6f and 7f over the winter months; never involved back on turf at Thirsk (7f, good) recently and although this is less competitive her stamina for a tough 7f like this still has to be proved.

races.paceDynamic: Applesandpears will dictate from the front with Lady Kodiac and Just A Girl likely to race prominently behind her, creating a modest but sustainable early gallop. With only one confirmed front-runner and limited early pressure, Applesandpears should get comfortable fractions through the first half of this 7f contest. The lack of genuine pace pressure means the race will develop into a tactical affair where positioning becomes crucial in the straight. This pace setup clearly favours hold-up horses who can pick up the pieces from off the pace, particularly those with finishing kicks over this trip.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front End
scenarios.trigger: If Applesandpears gets uncontested fractions and Lady Kodiac/Just A Girl don't apply early pressure
scenarios.body: The pace becomes too slow for closers to make up ground and prominent runners get first run in the straight. Those racing within striking distance can capitalize on the lack of finishing kick from behind.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closing Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely steady and the field bunches up turning for home
scenarios.body: Hold-up horses with proven finishing speed can exploit the slow pace by unleashing late runs. The race becomes a sprint from the 2f pole where class and acceleration matter most.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mid Race Injection
scenarios.trigger: If Lady Kodiac or Just A Girl decide to challenge Applesandpears before the turn
scenarios.body: The increased pace stretches the field and creates a more honest gallop that suits horses with tactical speed. Those able to travel strongly in midfield can strike at the right moment.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Applesandpears stops quickly after setting the pace and prominent runners struggle
scenarios.body: The race falls apart from the front creating opportunities for any horse with a turn of foot regardless of position. Form and class become the primary factors in a messy finish.

watchPoints.text: Applesandpears must be monitored for early pace judgment as she has been keen in the past and could set it up for closers
Lady Kodiac's positioning in the first furlong will indicate whether she applies pressure or settles behind the leader
Albaydaa's early movement with Marquand aboard could signal connections' confidence in her fitness after 22 days off
Orchid's ability to stay this trip remains questionable given her recent struggles beyond 6f on turf
Just A Girl's tactical approach with Osborne will show whether she races more patiently than recent efforts

races.name: Betway Bet £10 Get £60 Handicap

runners_data.name: St Anton
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner with proven class but faces five dedicated hold-up horses who will benefit from his honest gallop
runners_data.spotlight: Has proved reliable and progressive in his short career to date; got up near finish when winning at Newmarket (1m, good to firm) last month; that looks solid form and he may not have reached his ceiling just yet.

runners_data.name: Factual
runners_data.note: Strong closer making handicap debut for top trainer-jockey combination, represents significant potential improvement
runners_data.comment: Finished well when fourth of 12 on handicap debut at Chester; leading contender
runners_data.spotlight: Finished well when fourth of 12 on handicap debut at Chester (extended 7f, good) three weeks ago; remains open to improvement and this stiffer track should be in his favour; leading contender.

runners_data.name: Secret History
runners_data.note: Improving filly with good tactical speed who can sit prominent and get first run on the closers
runners_data.spotlight: Placed all four starts and she has won her last two; further improvement when coming from the rear to beat seven rivals at Wetherby (7f, good; hooded) five weeks ago; should stay today's extra yardage and there's almost certainly still better still to come.

runners_data.name: Sovereign View
runners_data.note: Solid each-way chance but poor trainer form and long absence since turf debut raise concerns
runners_data.spotlight: Steadily progressive; won Newcastle nursery last autumn and went down narrowly in Southwell handicap on reappearance; both those runs over 1m on AW (ran respectably on only turf outing); may be ready for a step up in distance but should still be thereabouts.

runners_data.name: Blue To Blue
runners_data.note: Consistent performer with strong recent form but claiming jockey is a negative in competitive handicap
runners_data.spotlight: Won three times for Karl Burke as a 2yo and ran a cracker when second at Haydock (1m, good) three weeks ago; hard to knock but he has had more goes than most of these and he was nudged up 2lb after Haydock.

runners_data.name: Horu Kanu
runners_data.note: Difficult ride who needs everything to fall right, cheekpieces may help but low-grade form is concerning
runners_data.spotlight: 0-6 and can look a difficult ride; rallied into third at Hamilton (1m, good) two weeks ago; needs to be sweetened up by cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Kanishka
runners_data.note: Frame candidate only, lacks the turn of foot needed to win off this break and moderate recent efforts
runners_data.spotlight: In frame all three runs this year, although he didn't go with much fluency when fourth of six at Musselburgh (1m; wore cheekpieces) on latest; more required against some unexposed rivals.

runners_data.name: Wild Thoughts
runners_data.note: Four-timer seeking horse whose rapid mark rise may have caught up with him against stronger opposition
runners_data.spotlight: Unbeaten in four races since tackling handicaps, his mark rising from 56 to 84; again had plenty in hand when beating 11 rivals at Windsor (1m, good to firm); impossible to rule out another step forward.

races.paceDynamic: St Anton will be the primary pace-setter from the gates, with Secret History and Sovereign View likely to track close behind in prominent positions. The hold-up quartet of Factual, Blue To Blue, Horu Kanu, Kanishka and Wild Thoughts will settle towards the rear, creating a clear split between front and back runners. With only one confirmed front-runner in St Anton, he's unlikely to face early pressure and can dictate a measured gallop. This race shape strongly favours the hold-up horses who can unleash finishing kicks off what should be a sustainable pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If St Anton sets uncontested fractions and the pace becomes pedestrian
scenarios.body: The closers get perfect conditions to unleash their turns of foot in the final two furlongs. Multiple hold-up horses can quicken simultaneously off the steady gallop.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Secret History or Sovereign View can get first run on the field
scenarios.body: The winner gets away from the field before the hold-up horses can respond. St Anton's honest gallop sets up the race but he lacks the class edge at the weights.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If St Anton kicks clear turning for home and the hold-up horses fail to quicken
scenarios.body: The leader's class advantage proves decisive when he finds another gear. The closers are caught flat-footed by the change of pace from the front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop becomes crawling and turns into a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure speed test over the final three furlongs. The most naturally quick horses benefit regardless of their usual running style.

watchPoints.text: Wild Thoughts trading short despite rising 28lb in ratings - market confidence could signal another gear
St Anton's early position crucial - if others join him up front the race complexion changes completely
Secret History and Sovereign View both need to avoid getting trapped behind the slow early pace
Blue To Blue's 5lb claimer Jack Nicholls must time his move perfectly against stronger opposition
Factual represents the Andrew Balding stable who excel with lightly-raced improvers in competitive handicaps

races.name: Betway Good Luck Arsenal Handicap

runners_data.name: Count Palatine
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who thrives on stiff tracks like Carlisle and showed course form when winning over 7f here
runners_data.comment: Won sole course start (7f); improved as 4yo but well held in two runs this year
runners_data.spotlight: Useful effort in defeat at Beverley (about 7f) last May and confirmed that stiff tracks suit when winning here (7f, good to firm; sole course start) in August; improved again when successful at Ayr later and no surprise if he comes on plenty from first two runs in 2026.

runners_data.name: Candonomore
runners_data.note: Confirmed stayer who won over 1m at Bath and handles the distance, suits patient tactics from Rossa Ryan
runners_data.comment: Ready Bath win (1m) in April; similar form when 3rd for new yard latest; career-high mark
runners_data.spotlight: A ready winner at Bath (1m, firm) in April and, having run well over 1m2f in the past, he didn't have  a problem with 1m1f when a close third, just behind Ayr Poet, at Ayr since on yard debut; remains on a career-high mark though so a shade more may be needed.

runners_data.name: Mr King
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with finishing concerns and modest strike-rate, though capable of running well in competitive events
runners_data.spotlight: Modest 2-26 strike-rate and refused to race once in the autumn; however, he's often run well in competitive races, as when third of 19 at York (1m, good) last July and was hampered next time; creditable return for new yard at Redcar (first-time hood, cheekpieces now refitted) this month; involved.

runners_data.name: Freddie Steady Go
runners_data.note: Recent winner who stays well and suits the step up in trip with Tom Eaves able to time his challenge
runners_data.comment: Bumper winner; two minor Flat runs then made all over 7f here latest; has some potential
runners_data.spotlight: Cosy winner of minor bumper (good) on debut; had wind surgery after a moderate hurdle debut and, following a couple of fair Flat runs, he caught his rivals on the hop when making all over 7f here (soft) recently; has more to prove off his opening mark but should have some potential.

runners_data.name: Moon Beginnings
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with fading tendencies who needs to be ridden more positively to avoid late collapse
runners_data.comment: Winning debut over 7f last autumn; disappointing in handicaps since; cheekpieces on
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly raced; sole win came over 7f at Chester last September and he's shown only the odd glimmer of promise in handicaps on AW and turf since; falling quickly in the weights but cheekpieces have a big job to do.

runners_data.name: Jez Bomb
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer in good form this year who will appreciate the return to 1m after struggling over longer trips
runners_data.spotlight: Four wins in 2025 and he wasn't far away over 1m1f here in September; in reasonable form this year and this trip will suit better than the 1m4f he ran over at York last time out but it will be a good effort if he can win this off his current mark.

runners_data.name: Ayr Poet
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in excellent recent form but now 6lb higher than his last win and facing a stiff task
runners_data.comment: Has course form; excellent second at Ayr last week; now 6lb higher than latest win
runners_data.spotlight: All 13 wins have come elsewhere but he does have course form and he did so well when going close at Ayr (1m1f, good to firm) last week; however, he's now 6lb higher than his September win which might be a step too far.

runners_data.name: Eupator
runners_data.note: Front-runner without blinkers for the first time since his AW wins, returning after a 33-day break
runners_data.spotlight: Two front-running wins on Wolverhampton AW (about 1m and 1m1f) early in 2026; no impact behind Candonomore back on turf at Bath last time, when regular blinkers were left off, as today; likely other days.

runners_data.name: Priapos
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has found form over 1m for new trainer Phillip Makin after two AW wins late last year
runners_data.comment: Two AW wins at 1m in late 2025; promising on turf since back from break; can go well
runners_data.spotlight: Has done well over 1m for new connections, finding plenty for two wins on sand at Newcastle in late 2025; given a break after and two turf runs since, at Beverley and when fourth at Ayr ten days ago, suggest he isn't just an AW pony; can go well.

runners_data.name: Elizabeth Bay
runners_data.note: Prominent runner dropping significantly in grade but stamina concerns over this longer trip under pressure
runners_data.spotlight: Finished close up in 7f events on the AW for previous trainer but two handicap runs either side of a break were disappointing and her stamina will be under pressure back on this track.

runners_data.name: Marry The Night
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who has won three times on AW but now 15lb higher than his last turf appearance
runners_data.spotlight: Three 1m wins on Southwell AW this year; has also won on turf but he's 15lb higher than when last seen on grass in the autumn so needs to show his form on this surface can keep pace with the AW improvement.

races.paceDynamic: Eupator will take them along from the front as the only confirmed pace-setter, likely setting a manageable gallop without pressure from Ayr Poet and Elizabeth Bay who can track prominently. The lack of early speed means the tempo will build gradually through the middle sections before quickening from the 3f pole. With most runners coming from off the pace including Count Palatine, Candonomore, and Mr King, this sets up perfectly for hold-up horses who can finish strongly. This race shape clearly favours the patient hold-up merchants who can capitalise on the modest early gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Eupator sets uncontested fractions and the pace builds late.
scenarios.body: The patient closers get the perfect set-up to unleash their finishing kicks from the back, with plenty left in the tank for a sustained drive. Those held up can pick off the early leaders who've had to do too much work in front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runners Steal March
scenarios.trigger: If Eupator maintains a strong gallop and isn't caught by the closers.
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace pressure allows Eupator to dictate terms and kick clear when the field comes under pressure, with prominent runners like Ayr Poet staying on. The hold-up horses find themselves with too much ground to make up in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mid-Division Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and those tracking just behind take over.
scenarios.body: Runners like Moon Beginnings and Elizabeth Bay who sit in behind the leader can time their move perfectly when Eupator weakens. They avoid the traffic problems that affect the back markers while having enough left to outsprint the tired pace-setters.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Muddle
scenarios.trigger: If jockeys get the fractions wrong and create a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: The modest pace becomes a crawl before exploding into a cavalry charge where positioning matters more than running style. This creates chaos where any horse in the right place at the right time can capitalise regardless of their preferred tactics.

watchPoints.text: Eupator without his regular blinkers could either improve or lose focus as the only pace-setter
Moon Beginnings and Mr King both show fading tendencies in the finish which could be exposed in a slowly-run race
Count Palatine returning to Carlisle where he won over 7f and the stiff track should suit his finishing kick
Ayr Poet racing off a 6lb higher mark than his last win and may find this tougher despite recent good form
Priapos and Marry The Night both returning to turf after AW success and need to prove the form translates
